title: Bound on the Value of a Canonical Suffix
statement: Let $w$ be a Boolean word, let $n,j\in\mathbb{N}$, and suppose that $w$ is empty or its last bit is true. If the length of $w$ is at most the binary bit length of $n$, then the value represented by the suffix of $w$ after dropping its first $j$ bits is at most $2n$.
